*The only solution which we can suggest is to turn off HEIC format file upload to Expense Reports (cc:* [~accountid:63184a39316bbc56c425dacf]*).* 

Please let me know if this solution works for you. Unfortunately based on technical limitations, there is nothing more we can offer. I’m attaching also the whole discussion about this case with our developers for your insights: 

# The HEIC format is a fairly recent format for images mainly used by the newest generations of iOS devices such as iPhones. Unfortunately, the integration uses BIRT (the Workday Studio tool used to convert data from WD into PDfs) and this tool does not allow the HEIC format.
Some solutions I have found by researching Community are:
# Asking workers not to use this format, iPhones allow this. Also, if you use the Workday application in the device, the uploaded photo should be a usable format. You can check this in the discussion: [https://community.workday.com/question/1175033?check_logged_in=1|https://community.workday.com/question/1175033?check_logged_in=1]
# Heavy research on the topic of HEIC format for integrations and found out the following:

* Workday as a cloud software supports HEIC images as long as the web browser you are using supports this format.
* Workday is able to encode HEIC files into base64 format to be used in a RaaS report for integrations.
* Workday Studio is not able to open a base64 formatted HEIC file as an image (like it does for the other types of file formats, except PDF, in INT011).
* Workday Studio is not able to decode a base64 formatted HEIC file into pdf.

*Since Workday Studio is not able to work with HEIC files, we cannot include them in the integration.* Workday *does not currently* offer a workaround for managing this type of files. The most probable reason why WD does not is because HEIC is a recent format which is originally intended to be only used in mobile devices for high quality pictures and space saving, so it is not intended to be used in integrations across platforms. *I suggest that you wait for a WD delivered solution/workaround and try advising your employees to not upload this type of files.*

*Supreme Administrative Court in Finland classified couriers as employees*

* The Supreme Administrative Court in Finland has ruled that food delivery couriers working via a platform (Wolt) are employees, not independent contractors.
* While couriers could choose their hours, reject tasks, decide how to perform deliveries, and use substitutes, the court found that all criteria of an employment relationship under Finnish law were still met.
* Wolt exercised direction and supervision through its platform, using data to monitor performance and enforce quality standards. It could also reduce pay or terminate agreements based on performance metrics or user feedback.
* As a result, increased scrutiny from authorities and more claims from couriers are expected.

More information on the ruling can be found here: [Summary: Supreme Administrative Court of Finland - Wolt couriers 2025|https://docs.google.com/document/d/17F5zSvuhFY_LCUKD5killrZ4skoQ8GnesfbHySXj0tE/edit?tab=t.0].

Braze automatically records key metrics such as timestamp, notification content, delivery status, and recipient counts, allowing Bolt to demonstrate when, how, and to whom user notifications were issued. * Together, the Excel register, Data Breach Report, and Braze logs collectively provide evidence of Bolt’s notification practices, though they are not consolidated into a single MODA-style “清冊” roster. *Assessment:* *Observations:* * Partially aligned. {code:sql}with facr_flags as (
  select
    etl.order_id as order_id,
    etl.city_id as city_id,
    MAX(CASE WHEN facr."type" = 'SAME_RIDER_DRIVER_PHONE' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS has_flag
  from ng_public.fraud_order_check as fac 
left join ng_public.fraud_order_check_result as facr ON facr.order_check_id = fac.id 
and facr.created_date >= CAST(DATE_ADD('month', -1, current_date) AS date)
  JOIN ng_public.etl_denormalized_commerce_orders AS etl ON fac.city_id = etl.city_id AND fac.order_id = etl.order_id AND fac.user_id = etl.user_id
  where fac.created_date >= CAST(DATE_ADD('month', -1, current_date) AS date)
  and etl.created_date >= CAST(DATE_ADD('month', -1, current_date) AS date)
  GROUP BY 1,2
)
select
etl.country_code,
count(distinct etl.order_id) as private_match_count,
count(distinct CASE WHEN ff.has_flag = 1 THEN etl.order_id END) AS SAME_RIDER_DRIVER_PHONE_count,
count(distinct CASE WHEN ff.has_flag = 0 THEN etl.order_id END) AS no_flag_count,
--
sum(etl.partner_price_eur) as partner_price_eur,
sum(etl.initial_failed_payment_amount/etl.eur_currency_rate) as initial_failed,
sum(etl.current_failed_payment_amount/etl.eur_currency_rate) as failed_pay_sum,
sum(etl.initial_chargeback_amount/etl.eur_currency_rate) as CB_sum,
sum(etl.refund_amount/etl.eur_currency_rate) as refund_sum,
sum(etl.bonus_amount/etl.eur_currency_rate) as bonus_sum,
sum(etl.tips_amount/etl.eur_currency_rate) as tips_sum
FROM ng_public.etl_denormalized_commerce_orders AS etl
left join facr_flags as ff on ff.order_id = etl.order_id and ff.city_id = etl.city_id
left join ng_pii.fleet_driver as d on d.id = etl.driver_courier_id
and d.created_date >= CAST(DATE_ADD('year', -5, CURRENT_DATE) AS DATE)
left join ng_pii.user_user AS uu ON uu.id = etl.user_id
and uu.created_date >= CAST(DATE_ADD('year', -5, CURRENT_DATE) AS DATE)
inner join ng_public.fleet_driver_root as dr
  ON d.driver_root_id = dr.id
  and (uu.phone <> dr.phone and uu.phone = dr.private_phone)
  where 1 = 1
  and etl.created_date >= CAST(DATE_ADD('month', -1, CURRENT_DATE) AS DATE)
  and dr.created_date >= CAST(DATE_ADD('year', -5, CURRENT_DATE) AS DATE)
  --
  and uu.phone <> dr.phone and uu.phone = dr.private_phone
  and etl.order_state = 'finished' and etl.order_type = 'rides'
  group by 1
  order by 3 desc{code}

Hi team, 

The user is reporting a double-charge because of incremental authorization.
Incremental authorization in card payments refers to the process of requesting an additional authorization on a customer’s card when the original authorized amount is insufficient to cover the final transaction cost. This typically happens in scenarios where the final amount of the transaction is not known upfront or may change.

I have checked the case and everything looks good on Bolt’s end. The pre-authorization has been released to the customer. 
You can ask the customer to reach out to their bank in order to confirm the authorized funds have been released. Their bank can locate the funds with the authorization date and amount.
